anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions serialize on hot buffer pages, latches, or page-pin slots inside the buffer manager, leading to CPU spin or waits while pages are being read, written, or flushed.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The physical storage layer is unable to sustain the read/write volume demanded by the engine, causing backlog, high latency, and prolonged I/O waits.

When both issues surface simultaneously, the database exhibits a compounded symptom set: severe and erratic response-time spikes, high buffer-busy and page-latch waits co-existing with swollen read/write wait times, CPU cores oscillating between spin-loops and idleness, log-write stalls, and checkpoint or bulk-load operations overrunning their windows. Buffer pages grow scarce because they take longer to be written back; sessions then thrash on the remaining hot pages, intensifying latch contention. Wait-event histograms show interleaved latch-related and I/O-related waits, making isolation of a single culprit difficult.

Causally, saturated storage slows page flushes and read-ins, lengthening the residency of dirty pages and inflating buffer churn. The reduced recycling rate leaves fewer clean frames, forcing more sessions to compete for the same hot pages and their protecting latches. In turn, the heavier latch contention stalls user work, producing bursty I/O patterns (e.g., massed retry reads or redo flush surges) that further overload the storage subsystem. The feedback loop between slow physical I/O and in-memory latch bottlenecks amplifies both anomalies, degrading throughput and stability across OLTP and analytical workloads.

entry.official_description: Unable to read the existing undo truncate log file '%s'. The error is %s
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
